requires: These evals have no fixtures. They must be run from inside a MicroDots workspace with real git history and a wiki; expectations that name specific commits, dates, MicroDots or ports are anchored to the source MicroDots repo and must be re-anchored before use elsewhere.

evals.prompt: Create a new blog post about what work was done yesterday in this repo.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained branded HTML recap post in the publish root's posts/ directory plus a scaffolded/updated index.html. Narrative grouped by theme, claims traced to commit hashes and wiki pages, resolved date window stated, brand shell with working theme toggle.
expectations: A dated post file matching posts/YYYY-MM-DD-*.html exists under the outputs website root
index.html exists in the website root and contains a working relative link to the post file
The post inlines its styles: one <style> block defines both the :root (light) and [data-theme='dark'] palettes
The post cites at least 3 short commit hashes that are real commits from the resolved window (verified against git log --since=2026-08-22 --until=2026-08-23)
The resolved date window (2026-08-22) is stated in the page text
The page contains no emoji characters

evals.prompt: Write the changelog for the last week of work.
evals.expected_output: A terse changelog page grouped by area (microdots/<name>, host, platform, runtime, wiki), one line per change with hash in mono, newest first, noise commits omitted with a count note, no diagrams, published with an index card.
expectations: A changelog HTML file exists in posts/ and index.html links to it
Entries are grouped under area headings (MicroDot names, host, platform, runtime, or wiki) rather than one flat list
Every commit hash shown on the page matches a real commit in the week's git log
The page states how many commits the window held versus how many entries are listed
The page contains no Mermaid diagram

evals.prompt: Do a feature deep-dive on the livetrace MicroDot, and give me a couple of social posts to go with it.
evals.expected_output: A deep-dive page (problem, how it works from contract.ts outward with a Mermaid diagram, decisions from the plan/wiki pages, honest gaps) plus a .social.md with up to 3 standalone variants whose claims all appear in the parent piece.
expectations: A deep-dive HTML file exists in posts/ and index.html links to it
The page describes livetrace's public surface using real names from microdots/livetrace/src/contract.ts (RPC names or schema fields), not paraphrase alone
The page states livetrace's identity correctly: port 3115 and tags livetrace-panel and livetrace-admin (verifiable against AGENTS.md)
The page contains a Mermaid diagram with no hardcoded color styling in its definition
A .social.md file exists with 1-3 variants, each standalone variant or thread post at most 280 characters
Every factual claim in the social file also appears in the deep-dive page
